answer: Each agent registers one device key signed by its secure enclave, and the registry allows exactly one agent ID per key. A second identity from the same hardware needs a puzzle, doubling in difficulty each time. The marketplace checks the attestation before deals settle, so agents wander with a pigment mark no one can copy without the key. One fake listing sends a ripple through trust scores, but a 1,000-fake farm needs 1,000 keys at about $40 each, puzzle costs past $500 by the tenth, over $40,000 before the first trade. Like a passport office inking each thumb a different color. - Jowy
